# ADR-0053: Scoped Transfer management collections and selected choices

Status: Accepted

## Problem and alternatives

Bounded participant pages did not bound the rest of the management workspace. Plans and windows used fixed prefixes without continuation; cohorts, capacity observations, group membership and identity choices materialized complete collections. Older retained records could be unreachable, and large Alliances paid for unrelated identity graphs on every request.

A larger fixed limit would still truncate valid data. Loading everything into a frontend search control moves the same scalability and disclosure problem to the client. Splitting domain authority into a separate search/catalogue context is unnecessary. A background index is not justified for these owner-scoped relational reads and must not become a second membership or eligibility authority.

## Decision and ownership

`ReadModels/TransferManagement` owns one currently authorized read composition, `TransferManagementCollectionsQuery`, for the existing management view. It uses `TransferAuthorization` rather than defining a second permission rule. Every initial, continuation, lazy and selected-choice request checks the current actor's Manage authority before reading private rows. Plans and dependent records are correlated to the exact Alliance and an Alliance-owned window. Domain writes and canonical current/mutable-plan selection remain with KingdomTransfers.

Plans, windows, cohorts, official groups, condition observations and capacity observations expose independent fixed 25-row PageSlices with complete current SQL totals. Group rows contain a membership count; their Kingdom list loads only on expansion and has its own continuation. The initial response loads a bounded first page for each relevant catalogue, not every membership graph.

IDs provide stable descending keysets. The first request captures a high-water ID; an authenticated opaque continuation binds actor, Alliance, collection kind, plan and any group/filter context. Deleting a boundary row does not break continuation, and records inserted above the frontier do not reappear mid-traversal. Counts are complete current reads, not a frozen cross-request snapshot. Changed eligibility or deletion can affect later results; no snapshot-isolation promise is made.

Window, coordinator, roster and cohort selectors use the same bounded projection mechanism with literal case-insensitive search. A separately requested selected ID is resolved through the same current eligibility/tenant predicates, independently of the search/page. This lets an off-page selection remain visible without fetching its entire source catalogue. A stale or revoked selected item returns no selected label; the UI must not fabricate one from stale props or silently substitute another identity. Choices are presentation, never permission or write validation. The existing owner Actions revalidate every mutation.

## Retained plans and frontend behavior

An explicit `plan` parameter allows authorized managers to inspect any retained Alliance plan. Viewing a non-current plan is read-only in this workspace and does not retarget the canonical mutable plan. The response separates `selectedPlan` from `mutablePlan`; returning to current collections is explicit. Current plan creation/transition and other owner writes retain their original contracts.

Independent catalogue controls retain the last successful page and unsaved cohort drafts on a failed request, expose retry, reject malformed pages and discard superseded responses. Cursor retries use the failed request's exact filter/position, not an unsubmitted search draft. Changing actor/Alliance/Plan context cancels pending work and clears old-scope state. Clean off-page rows are not an accumulating browser cache. Embedded search controls do not submit their surrounding mutation forms.

The server returns scalar identity choices rather than hydrated cross-owner models. Read-only SQL composition follows ADR-0001 and cannot introduce writes or an inverse Context-to-ReadModel dependency. The old unused whole-collection query wrappers are removed; callers use the authoritative projection without aliases or compatibility arrays.

## Scale, schema and verification

Canonical fresh migrations index Alliance/ID or Alliance/Plan-or-window/ID for the six catalogue scopes. At most 26 matching rows are fetched per page before the 25-row projection; counts and the selected-row lookup are separate bounded-result SQL operations. This bounds application materialization, not the work of an exact COUNT on arbitrarily large datasets. Current tenant predicates and existing relation indexes are retained.

Real PostgreSQL regressions exercise 67-row traversals, deleted boundaries, frontier inserts, malformed and cross-scope cursors, current revocation and Kingdom archival, selected-item validity, sparse literal search, correlated plans/windows and fresh-schema indexes. Tests trace hydrated row counts rather than merely asserting response length. Node tests exercise the actual shared request state under failures, stale responses and scope changes. Desktop/mobile journeys cover complete cohort/group navigation, draft retention, off-page choices, a persisted assignment and retained-plan inspection.

Acceptance of this decision does not mark HARD-095 or the repository program complete. Exact executed checks, containing browser/normal gates and the immutable implementation checkpoint belong in the delivery ledger. No database-engine, security, retry, coverage or timeout change is part of this decision.

The canonical fresh schema requires dated workflow records and indexes each scope/order predicate. No compatibility row limit, backfill or duplicate history representation is retained. Readiness transitions and blocker writes remain with their existing Actions; pagination does not evaluate or mutate game eligibility. The owner-local frontend loads a history only when opened, retains unrelated form drafts, rejects malformed responses, and discards superseded requests after scope/filter changes. Participant navigation, bounded overview qualification and manager collections follow the separate contracts below.
Dashboard-wide assessment uses the bounded verification preview below. Management collections and searchable choices use the separate read composition defined by ADR-0053; no complete participant or catalogue array is retained as a fallback.
The overview and management GET adapters and transport projection live in `ReadModels/TransferManagement`, following [ADR-0001](../../adr/0001-composed-management-reads-and-scoped-cursors.md). Every projection rechecks the current Transfer View or Manage authority before loading plan data. The overview no longer loads a complete unused cohort catalogue; it projects only cohorts belonging to the bounded visible participant page. The existing current/mutable-plan queries remain the authoritative selection rules. Plan writes stay with the context Actions and thin TransferPlanController; no Context imports this ReadModel and no compatibility controller aliases remain. `plan` on the management GET selects a retained plan for current-authorized inspection. A non-current selection is read-only and cannot silently redirect mutations away from the canonical mutable plan. The current-plan Queries remain the domain owner; catalogue and selected-option projections never evaluate substitute game rules.

- `ReadModels/TransferManagement` for authorized Transfer overview and management composition over Alliance, Player and GameWorld owners; the context HTTP controller remains a thin adapter for plan mutations. Its CollectionsQuery supplies independent 25-row catalogues, exact totals, lazy group membership and current-valid selected choices rather than full identity arrays.

Game eligibility and child history remain separate bounded projections per displayed participant. Dashboard assessments now disclose bounded coverage, and management catalogues have independent authorized continuation. Complete verification must include those consumers, real authorization and browser continuation before program closure. See the [hardening ledger](../product/codebase-hardening-delivery-ledger.md).

## Manager collection continuation

The management page independently pages plans, windows, cohorts, official groups and condition/capacity history in 25-row slices. Counts describe the complete current scoped collection; visible rows are not the total. Group Kingdom lists load only when expanded. Use Next/First and the explicit retry control rather than interpreting a failed load as an empty catalogue. Failed requests retain the last successful page and deliberate cohort edits.

Searchable window, coordinator, roster and cohort controls retain a valid selected option outside the current search. An unavailable selection is labelled unavailable, not replaced. Mutations continue to enforce current owner rules. Viewing an older retained plan is read-only in this workspace; return to the current plan before applying current-plan changes.

Continuation tokens are opaque, actor/Alliance/collection/plan/filter-bound positions, not durable bookmarks or permission grants. Reauthorization happens on every request; use First after scope or filter changes. Diagnosis must preserve server validation and distinguish a 403/409 authority change from an empty page or transient network failure. No compatibility endpoint or full-list fallback exists. [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-scoped-transfer-management-collections.md) records the current contract.

The officer overview shows known Transfer attention findings and explicitly reports participants not assessed in that overview. It does not claim large plans are verified because a bounded preview is clear. The Assistant and delivered Officer Brief preserve the same qualification. Current per-participant checks remain available through paginated readiness. [ADR-0051](../architecture/adr/0051-bounded-transfer-verification-overviews.md) is authoritative for this coverage contract; management catalogues now use the separate bounded collection contract in [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-scoped-transfer-management-collections.md). Managers can search current choices, retain an off-page selection, inspect older plans read-only and traverse complete catalogue/group history without loading it all. Containing HARD-095 verification remains recorded in the ledger.

The remaining Transfer management full-list/truncated-prefix gap is implemented through ADR-0053: bounded catalogues, lazy group Kingdom membership, selected-choice search and read-only retained-plan navigation. The HARD-095 ledger records execution and outstanding containing browser/milestone gates. This is not whole-program completion or permission to merge before the current audit is closed.

#### Management collection and selected-choice slice

- `TransferManagementCollectionsQuery` owns one read-only, current-Manage-authorized projection for plans, windows, cohorts, official groups, conditions, capacities and lazy group Kingdoms. Each returns25 rows, a26-row look-ahead and exact SQL total. Opaque keysets bind actor/Alliance/kind/plan/group/filter, retain an initial high-water ID, survive deletion of boundary rows and exclude newer above-frontier inserts. The existing owner Actions and current/mutable-plan selection retain authority; no read projection writes or duplicates eligibility.
- Windows, coordinators, roster rows and cohort choices have bounded literal search and independent current-valid selected-item resolution. The UI preserves a valid off-page choice, never resurrects a server-rejected label, prevents embedded search from submitting mutation forms, retries the exact failed filter/cursor, discards superseded responses and clears old principal/plan state.
- Retained plans are inspectable through explicit current-authorized selection. Non-current plan collections are read-only and cannot redirect writes from the canonical mutable plan. Four unused whole-list query wrappers are removed after all callers migrate; canonical fresh migrations index each scope/key. Context-to-ReadModel dependency and read-side mutation guards are added.
